explicit_assumptions: The reference is the equilibrium funicular for a two-hinged parabolic arch under a vertical load uniformly distributed over the horizontal span
The parent deck tributary loads are reduced to the same total vertical load W over the horizontal span L; no stiffness quantity enters the reference equations
Axis ordinate is measured from the straight line joining two equal-elevation arch feet, and rise f is the maximum positive ordinate
For DECK_ARCH the measured quantity is the BRD-042 foundation-thrust magnitude; for tied arches it is the positive DECK tie-force envelope
The reciprocal factor-five order band is a model-error alarm only and is not a code acceptance limit
explicit_limitations: This is a statics-only funicular reference and geometry diagnostic; it is not a second frame solver and does not satisfy project gate G4 by itself
The bending proxy is M0-H_ref*y_actual for the idealised uniform vertical load; it is not the F1 element moment and not a design action
The foundation-thrust or tie-force comparison checks sign and order of magnitude only; it does not establish accuracy, resistance, utilization or adequacy
Load redistribution by deck stiffness, spandrels, hangers, end posts and polygonal rib discretisation is absent from the reference model
No bearing, abutment, foundation or soil stiffness is represented, so H_ref is not a foundation design load
No self-weight generation, prestress, P-Delta, buckling, material nonlinearity, dynamics, wind, seismic, fatigue, construction stage or code combination
A source_ref, hash and clause_id establish provenance only; they do not prove engineering applicability
Any technical use still requires an independent solver benchmark and responsible engineer review
promotion_requirements: Review the funicular equations, sign convention, load-domain checks and normalization independently
Benchmark reaction, tie force and bending distribution against a separate trusted solver on canonical and asymmetric arches
Add non-uniform and moving-load thrust-line envelopes before using the metric to rank design alternatives
Introduce project-specific bearings, abutments, foundations, soil interaction, load combinations, stability and resistance before design use
